subject: chemistry
title: Equilibrium Adventure 2: Le Chatelier's principle
welcome_lead: Today you'll shift equilibrium by changing temperature, pressure and concentration.
meta_desc: Chemistry — Le Chatelier's principle, changes in T/p/[X], effect on K.
final_note: You learned Le Chatelier predicts equilibrium shifts to counter changes; only T changes Kc; pressure favours fewer gas moles; concentration changes shift the position but not K.

walkthroughs.body_html:
For A + B ⇌ C:

Add more A → forward rate ↑ → shifts right, making more C until new equilibrium. K unchanged.

Remove C → shifts right (replacing it).

Pressure (gases): system shifts to side with fewer moles of gas. N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃: 4 mol → 2 mol; high p favours NH₃.

Temperature: forward exothermic (ΔH < 0).
- Higher T → shifts back (endothermic), Kc decreases.
- Lower T → shifts forward, Kc increases.

Catalyst speeds both directions equally — no shift in position.

Haber process N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, ΔH = -92 kJ/mol.

Compromise: 450°C (not low — too slow), 200 atm (not higher — costly), Fe catalyst.
NH₃ continually removed → equilibrium drives further right.

Contact process: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃, ΔH = -197 kJ/mol. ~450°C, V₂O₅ catalyst, ~95% conversion.

mcqs.q: Increasing T on an exothermic reaction:
When a stress shifts an equilibrium, does the system fully undo the change?
options: No — Le Chatelier's principle says the system PARTIALLY opposes the change; equilibrium shifts to a new position that minimises but doesn't eliminate the disturbance.
The system shifts to completely cancel the change and return concentrations to their original values.
The system shifts to amplify the change because reactions always proceed in the disturbed direction.

mcqs.q: Does adding a catalyst change the value of Kc?
options: The system shifts to amplify the change because reactions always proceed in the disturbed direction.
A catalyst decreases Kc by stabilising the reactants.
A catalyst increases Kc by favouring product formation.
No — a catalyst speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally, so Kc is unchanged.

mcqs.q: What are the units of Kc for a reaction?
options: They depend on Δn (the difference between moles of gaseous/aqueous products and reactants) — Kc can be dimensionless or have units like mol dm^-3.
Kc always has units of mol dm^-3.
The system shifts to amplify the change because reactions always proceed in the disturbed direction.
